messages.subject: finance vs. utilitarian statistics projects
messages.body_plain:
What do mentors think of Stephen G Cecchetti & Enisse Kharroubi, 2015.
"Why does financial sector growth crowd out real economic growth?,"
BIS Working Papers 490, Bank for International Settlements.
http://www.bis.org/publ/work490.pdf ?

We've been asking Google to pay hundreds of thousands of dollars over
the years for projects which may be the most productive, to say the
least.

Is it fair to ask for ground rules to limit the proportion of finance
gsoc-r projects in favor of utilitarian general statistics?

messages.subject: Re: finance vs. utilitarian statistics projects
messages.body_plain:
On Wed, 2015-09-02 at 11:28 -0600, James Salsman wrote:
> Is it fair to ask for ground rules to limit the proportion of finance
> gsoc-r projects in favor of utilitarian general statistics?

I would beg to differ that 'utilitarian general statistics' is more
useful than the many different specialties that have been included in
our GSoC projects.  biostats, geostats, machine learning, optimization,
graphics have all been represented.

Google has given us more slots than we've used for each of the last
three years.

I think the challenge is getting good applications.

The best application are awarded slots.  Unprepared students and
incomplete applications happen in all types of projects.

Perhaps you should focus on getting better organized so that you can
attract talented mentors and students to your desired 'utilitarian'
projects.

Regards,

Brian
